SK Hynix is expected to present its own plan within the third quarter.

Start with whether the money is there, and the answer is plain.
Samsung's operating profit for the second quarter of 2026 was a record 89.5 trillion won, and net cash at the end of June stood at 167.59 trillion.
Net cash is the cash and equivalents on hand minus the debt that has to be repaid.

@@BAR@@Net cash, end of June|167.59 trillion won|167.59|Annual regular dividend|9.8 trillion won|9.8@@The pile is seventeen times one year of the regular dividend. That gap is where the talk of a special dividend comes from.@@Samsung Electronics Q2 2026 results and January 2024 shareholder return policy, retrieved 2026-08-13

## The current policy ends this year

@@TIME@@April 2021|A special dividend of 10.7 trillion won paid as the previous three-year policy closed|January 2024|The 2024-2026 policy announced, returning 50% of three-year free cash flow, with 9.8 trillion won a year in regular dividends|30 July 2026|Samsung tells its earnings call that the timing and the size are not decided|>Third quarter 2026|The window SK Hynix has given itself to fix an additional return plan@@The slot for a new policy is already on the calendar. This year is the last year of the current one.@@Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix disclosures and earnings materials, retrieved 2026-08-13

## Shareholders of higher-paying companies now owe less tax

To see why the question lands now, read one line of tax law.
From income accruing on 1 January 2026, dividend income is taxed separately in Korea.
Shareholders of a listed company that pays out more than 40% of profits are taxed at 14% to 35% on dividends on their own, rather than having them added to other income where the top rate is 45%.

@@REF@@Korean chipmakers face growing calls to improve shareholder returns (The Korea Times, 2026-08-10)|https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/business/companies/20260810/korean-chipmakers-face-growing-calls-to-improve-shareholder-returns|https://newsimg.koreatimes.co.kr/2026/08/10/fa755072-85dd-4c6b-8236-a7fc854ee267.jpg

If shareholders of a company that raises its payout owe less tax, the company gains a reason to raise it.
The same report adds the share price backdrop.
At the close on 7 August, Samsung was 36% below its June high and SK Hynix 51% below its own.

## SK Hynix answers first

The original post puts the two companies in one sentence, but they do not carry the same weight of confirmation.
SK Hynix said itself, alongside its quarterly dividend, that an additional return plan would be settled within the third quarter.
The Samsung half is a forecast in the Korean press, and the company said on its 30 July call only that it was reviewing options.
So the split is less about whether an announcement lands this month than about what is in it.
If the special dividend clears the 10.7 trillion won of 2021 and the payout ratio moves above the 50% of free cash flow line, this quarter's earnings are being shared; if the framework is simply carried over, the record cash stays inside the company.

The average decline was 1.2% in the first quarter of 2026, ending a 33-quarter run of increases that began in the fourth quarter of 2017.

@@REF@@Commercial insurance prices fell in first quarter: CIAB (Business Insurance, 2026-05-21)|https://www.businessinsurance.com/commercial-insurance-prices-fell-in-first-quarter-ciab/|https://www.businessinsurance.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/CIAB-chart.png

It collects how much prices moved when contracts came up for renewal, which is a different thing from the premium volume the industry actually collected.

@@CMP@@The common reading|Prices broke after 33 quarters, so the good years for insurers are over and revenue is starting to shrink.|What the gauge says|What fell is the price on renewing contracts. Industry net premiums written grew from $558.2 billion in 2017 to $929.8 billion in 2024.

Two numbers sitting in the same paragraph are measuring different things.
Renewal prices can fall while the total keeps rising, because the buildings and vehicles being insured are worth more and there are more of them.

## What exactly fell 1.2%

@@CHK@@Commercial property|-5.5%|Commercial auto|+5.8%|Small accounts|+1.1%@@Inside the single average, the parts moved in opposite directions. Cover on buildings and equipment fell hard, while cover for liability claims and for small firms went up.@@CIAB Commercial Property/Casualty Market Index, Q1 2026, retrieved 2026-08-13 (via Business Insurance)

## Property fell, liability rose

Property prices fell because money piled into the side that insures the insurers.
A carrier passes part of the risk it takes on to another company, and capital in that reinsurance market reached a record $790 billion in the first quarter of 2026.
Of that, $141 billion is alternative capital, the kind traded in the market like a bond.

@@REF@@Commercial P&C Market Shifts Into Reverse as Soft Market Takes Hold (Risk & Insurance, 2026-05-22)|https://riskandinsurance.com/commercial-pc-market-shifts-into-reverse-as-soft-market-takes-hold/|https://riskandinsurance.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/GettyImages-148271028.jpg

That report adds a second ingredient: insured natural catastrophe losses worldwide came in at $107 billion in 2025, below the prior year.

More capacity to absorb risk, less money going out the door, and the price comes down.
Commercial auto rates, meanwhile, are up for a 59th straight quarter.
Jury awards against companies keep climbing, so the cost of a single accident keeps rising.

## What AM Best expects for 2026

So the split is whether this marks the peak in insurer earnings or an adjustment confined to property.
The rating agency AM Best expects the US property and casualty combined ratio to rise from 95.0 in 2025 to 96.9 in 2026.
The combined ratio is claims and expenses measured against premiums collected, and anything under 100 means the underwriting itself makes money.
A move of nearly two points describes profit getting thinner, not profit disappearing.
If the next survey shows the overall rate negative again and small accounts turning down as well, the whole industry has moved into price cutting; if property keeps falling while liability keeps rising, one industry stays split in two.
jukan-coreweave-a100-2029-full-freight-v:
Reporting second-quarter results on August 11, CoreWeave said it had signed a contract on NVIDIA's A100, a chip from 2020, that runs to 2029, at full price.
In the same call it said it had raised rental prices across its lineup by about 25% in July.

@@REF@@CoreWeave raises prices 25% amid booming AI demand (Benzinga, 2026-08-12)|https://www.benzinga.com/markets/earnings/26/08/61133155/coreweave-25-percent-price-hike-vera-rubin-demand-ai|https://cdn.benzinga.com/cdn-cgi/image/width=1200,height=800,fit=crop/files/images/story/2026/08/12/Dhaka--Bangladesh-16-May-2025-Coreweave-.jpg

That report notes the increase came in two layers. The 25% raised against demand is one, and a pass-through of higher hardware costs sits on top of it.

@@IMG@@https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/03/NVIDIA_GPU.jpg/960px-NVIDIA_GPU.jpg|An A100 is an accelerator card that looks like this. A part released in 2020 is still turning up on rental contracts.|Mickael Courtiade · CC BY 2.0|https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:NVIDIA_GPU.jpg

## Why a GPU's lifespan is an earnings question

When a company buys $10 billion of equipment it does not book $10 billion of cost that year.
It spreads the cost across the years it expects to use the gear. That is depreciation.

One more step shows why this touches the share price.
Stretch the number of years and the cost booked each year falls, which makes that year's profit look larger.
How many years a company writes down for its equipment therefore sets the size of its reported profit.

Michael Burry aimed at exactly this in November 2025.
He argued that hyperscalers were understating depreciation by $176 billion across 2026 to 2028 by extending useful lives, and that this inflated Oracle's profit by 26.9% and Meta's by 20.8%.

@@TIME@@May 2020|NVIDIA A100 launches|Jan 2025|Meta extends server life from 4-5 years to 5.5, cutting 2025 depreciation by $2.9B|Jan 2025|Amazon shortens life on some servers from six years to five|Nov 2025|Burry argues hyperscalers are understating depreciation|>2029|CoreWeave's A100 contract runs out@@Companies moved in opposite directions on the same class of asset. The reason Amazon gave for shortening was that AI hardware is turning over faster.@@Company filings and press coverage (accessed 2026-08-13)

## What CoreWeave put on the table

The A100 launched in May 2020. A contract running to 2029 is nine years from that date.
Chief executive Mike Intrator said the deal was struck at full freight, meaning without a discount, and the finance chief said average selling prices on older generations are at or above where they sat a year ago.

The same release put second-quarter revenue at $2.575 billion, up 112% from a year earlier, with $104 billion of contracted work not yet recognised as revenue.
Active power rose by about 500 megawatts during the quarter to 1.5 gigawatts, and the year-end target was raised above 1.85 gigawatts.

All of these figures are CoreWeave's own disclosures. Who signed the contract, and what the price actually is, were not made public.

@@CMP@@The bear reading|GPUs lose usefulness within three or four years and leave nothing at resale, so stretching their book life inflates profit.|CoreWeave's reading|If somebody still wants to rent the older gear, it carries a price. Older-generation ASPs are running above last year.

The owner who runs the chip and the landlord who rents it out are reading different values off the same silicon.

## CoreWeave is not a hyperscaler

This is why a single contract does not settle it.
CoreWeave is paid by the hour to run other people's compute, so an older chip pays as long as it stays booked.
Meta and Oracle are using the gear to train their own models. When a newer chip does more work on the same electricity, the older one can be cheaper left idle.
The same chip in a different seat is worth a different amount.

There is one thing to watch. If more companies follow Amazon and shorten the life, CoreWeave's contract stays a fact about the rental business. If more follow Meta and stretch it, the reading that old GPUs still carry a price gets stronger.

bilello-gross-vs-net-interest-1_37t-soci:
Interest charged on US government debt over the past twelve months came to $1.37 trillion, a record.
But lining that number up against Social Security spending to see which is bigger does not work. The two are not measured with the same ruler.

@@REF@@US July deficit tops $432 billion as outlays grow (Reuters, 2026-08-12)|https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/policy/articles/us-july-deficit-tops-432-180448445.html|https://storage.googleapis.com/media.mwcradio.com/mimesis/2026-08/12/2026-08-12T180448Z_2_LYNXMPEM7B1FE_RTROPTP_3_USA-TRUMP-LABOR-SENATE.JPG

Reuters reports from the July Monthly Treasury Statement that the month's deficit was $432 billion, a July record, and that the fiscal 2026 shortfall over ten months is $1.799 trillion. Interest is the fastest-growing item inside that gap.

## Interest goes by two names

The "interest expense on the public debt" that Treasury publishes each month adds up the interest on every Treasury security outstanding.
That includes the interest on securities held by the Social Security and Medicare trust funds.

That portion is money the government moves from one pocket to another and writes down as interest.
No cash leaves the government, so the budget does not count it as interest at all.

What the budget carries instead is a different number, net interest, with that portion taken out.
Fiscal 2024 shows the gap plainly. Gross interest was $1.133 trillion and net interest was $880 billion.
In a single year, two figures both called interest sat $253 billion apart.

@@BAR@@Social Security outlays|$1.569T|1569|Gross interest|$1.229T|1229|Net interest in the budget|$1.028T|1028@@The figure Bilello cites is the trailing-twelve-month version of the middle bar. The one that competes with Social Security for size is the bottom bar.@@Fiscal 2025 actuals, CBO Monthly Budget Review (November 2025) and US Treasury Fiscal Data (accessed 2026-08-13)

## Net interest is already number two

Correcting the number does not shrink the story.
In fiscal 2025 Social Security was the largest line at $1.569 trillion, and net interest came next at $1.028 trillion.
Medicare at $992 billion and national defense at $868 billion sat below it.
Interest has already passed health care and defense to become the second-largest item in the budget.

The cause is not only a bigger pile of debt. The price of carrying it went up.
The average rate on marketable Treasury debt rose from 1.5% in July 2021 to 3.4% in July 2026, more than doubling.
Put simply, rolling the same stack of debt costs twice what it cost five years ago, and the stack grew as well.

## CBO does not see it by 2055 either

Everything turns on which ruler you pick up.
Measured gross, the gap to Social Security has already narrowed to under $200 billion and a crossover looks close.
Measured as the budget line, the Congressional Budget Office's long-term outlook puts net interest at 5.4% of gross domestic product in 2055 against 6.0% for Social Security. Three decades out, Social Security is still larger.
Mix the two figures and you get "soon to be first." Use one of them consistently and you get "still second in thirty years."
The books on this fiscal year close in mid-October.
meru-jackson-hole-2026-payments-theme-wa:
The Kansas City Fed has set the theme for this year's Jackson Hole symposium, held August 27 to 29. It is not interest rates. It is "Financial Innovation: Implications for Payments and Policy."

@@REF@@Jackson Hole Economic Policy Symposium (Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City, accessed 2026-08-13)|https://www.kansascityfed.org/research/jackson-hole-economic-symposium/|https://www.kansascityfed.org/images/GettyImages-1743180766.original.jpg

## The theme is the year's worry

Jackson Hole is a three-day gathering that the Kansas City Fed, one of the twelve regional Federal Reserve banks, has hosted since 1978.
Only about a hundred people are invited, mostly central bank governors and academic economists, and press access is kept deliberately small.
The Kansas City Fed also picks the theme, which is why the theme tends to show what the Fed is worrying about that year.

In 2024 it was "Reassessing the Effectiveness and Transmission of Monetary Policy." In 2025 it was "Labor Markets in Transition: Demographics, Productivity, and Macroeconomic Policy."
How far to move rates, and how work itself is changing, were the questions of the past two years.

This year it is payments.

One step of explanation makes clear why that belongs on a central bankers' agenda.
A stablecoin is a token that moves on a blockchain while its value is pinned one to one to a currency such as the dollar.
That is the definition, and the part central banks care about comes right after it.
Once people start paying each other with the token instead of through a bank account, the question of who controls the payment rails changes hands.
The channel a central bank uses to steer the economy also runs through bank deposits and bank lending, so money that circulates outside that channel is money policy reaches less easily.

## Warsh called it a blank page

Kevin Warsh was sworn in as Fed chair on May 22, 2026. This is his first Jackson Hole in the job.
Asked at the July 29 FOMC press conference how he was preparing the speech, he said it looked to him "like a blank piece of paper right now," and that he had not begun consideration.
He added that he would like to raise some big questions. He did not say which ones.

@@REF@@Cooler CPI inflation reading bolsters case for Fed to hold rates in September (Yahoo Finance, 2026-08-12)|https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/policy/article/cooler-cpi-inflation-reading-bolsters-case-for-fed-to-hold-rates-in-september-125312469.html|https://s.yimg.com/lo/mysterio/api/56C61E219630EA23B9CA351F744A01A1F766EE96B1B752C2747A4AB587F86A8B/subgraphmysterio/resizefill_w1200_h900;quality_80;format_webp/https:%2F%2Fs.yimg.com%2Fos%2Fcreatr-uploaded-images%2F2026-07%2F03b87200-8757-11f1-a754-7e31ab63180a

That report notes that July consumer prices, published August 12, rose 3.4% from a year earlier against 3.5% in June, and that core prices excluding food and energy eased to 2.5%, pushing the market toward expecting no change at the September meeting.
Right after the release, the probability attached to a hold sat near 55%.

@@TIME@@Aug 12|July CPI published, inflation eases|>Aug 27-29|Jackson Hole symposium, official theme is payments|>Aug 28|By custom, the chair speaks on this day|>Sep 16|FOMC rate decision@@The chair's Jackson Hole speech is the last set-piece the market gets before the September meeting, and this year it belongs to someone standing there for the first time.@@Kansas City Fed symposium page and Federal Reserve Board 2026 meeting calendar (accessed 2026-08-13)

## What Warsh says before September 16

Two things split here.
If Warsh gives any signal about the September path, the market reprices that day. There is no forward guidance in place right now, meaning no standing language about the next meeting, so the further the signal sits from consensus the larger the move.
If instead the three days stay on payments and stablecoin rules, rate expectations drift where they are until September 16 without a direction.
Which one it is becomes clear on August 28.
serenity-nbis-prepayments-cover-half-of-:
Nebius booked $582.3 million in the second quarter.
That is 454% more than a year earlier, and capex in the same quarter came to $5.7 billion.

@@REF@@NVIDIA-backed Nebius says AI capacity demand is so hot it could sell out 2027 today (Benzinga, 2026-08-12)|https://www.benzinga.com/markets/earnings/26/08/61139317/nvidia-backed-nebius-says-ai-capacity-demand-is-so-hot-it-could-sell-out-2027-today|https://cdn.benzinga.com/cdn-cgi/image/width=1200,height=800,fit=crop/files/images/story/2026/08/12/Nebius-Group.jpg

Nebius buys NVIDIA chips, installs them in data centers, and rents the compute out by the hour.
There is always one sore spot in that arithmetic.
The money for chips and buildings leaves first, and the rent comes back spread over years.

## The customer pays first

Around 70% of second-quarter contracts carried customer prepayments, and the company says those prepayments cover 50% to 60% of the related capex.
A prepayment is money handed over before the thing is delivered.
Instead of the builder borrowing from a bank and repaying later, the tenant puts up half the construction cost in advance.

@@REF@@Nebius revenue surges as AI cloud margins climb in Q2 2026 (Blockspace, 2026-08-12)|https://blockspace.media/insight/nebius-revenue-surges-ai-cloud-margins-q2-2026/

That report puts second-quarter adjusted EBITDA at $236.2 million and the margin at 41%, up from 32% in the first quarter.
Cash from operations came to $2.3 billion.
This is why a company spending far more than it earns still ended June with $8 billion on hand.

The risk has not disappeared, though. It has moved.
If a customer that paid in advance cannot carry the contract to the end, what remains on the other side is a finished building and chips already bought.

## Power gets locked in before revenue does

The company lifted its year-end contracted power target from more than 4 gigawatts to 5 gigawatts.
The source post reports short-term deals being priced above $40 million per megawatt per year.

@@TIME@@2026-03-31|Annual recurring revenue $1.9B|2026-06-30|Annual recurring revenue $3.0B, cash $8B|2026-07|Raises a $775M loan facility due October 2030|>2026-12|Contracted power of 5 gigawatts|>2027|More than 1 gigawatt brought online each year@@Power is locked in contracts years ahead, while revenue only lands once equipment sits behind that power. The pace of this company is set by electricity rather than by orders.@@Nebius Q2 2026 results and related coverage, retrieved 2026-08-12

## What Nebius has to show in early 2027

So where does this growth get confirmed.
The company kept its 2026 revenue guidance of $3.0 billion to $3.4 billion and a year-end annual recurring revenue target of $7 billion to $9 billion.
Annual recurring revenue is what the contracts already signed would produce if they ran for a full year.

Getting from $3.0 billion at the end of June to $7 billion by year-end means more than doubling again across two quarters.
Reach it and the story of building on prepayments and selling what was built holds up; fall short and the reading is that power was locked in ahead of demand that did not arrive as quickly.
Whether the $9 billion of prepayments lands on schedule is the signal that shows up first, quarter by quarter, in the meantime.
kobeissi-leveraged-etf-16pct-turnover-1p:
Leveraged ETFs are producing 16% of the money that changes hands across global ETFs each day.
The assets behind them come to $250 billion, 1% of a $22 trillion market.

@@BAR@@Share of daily trading value|16%|16|Share of total assets|1%|1@@The sixteen-fold gap is about speed rather than size. The same dollar is bought and sold far more often here than in the rest of the ETF market.@@The Kobeissi Letter tally, posted 2026-08-12

A leveraged ETF is built to follow two or three times the daily move of an index or a single stock.

Because that multiple has to be reset every day, the fund buys more after an up day and sells more after a down day.
The bigger these funds get, the more orders pile into the same direction near the close.

## Assets fell while turnover accelerated

@@REF@@1H 2026 Market Structure and Flows (Citadel Securities, 2026-06-30)|https://www.citadelsecurities.com/news-and-insights/global-market-intelligence/1h-2026-market-structure-flows/|https://www.citadelsecurities.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/06/SR28-cover.jpg

Citadel Securities counted about $218 billion of leveraged ETF assets at the end of June.
Roughly $82 billion, or 60%, of that arrived in the second quarter alone, with semiconductor products up 175%.

@@REF@@Leveraged ETF boom creates new ways to profit from sudden bursts of volatility (WealthManagement, 2026-08-10)|https://www.wealthmanagement.com/etfs/leveraged-etf-boom-creates-new-ways-to-profit-from-sudden-bursts-of-volatility|https://eu-images.contentstack.com/v3/assets/bltabaa95ef14172c61/blt4fff1cb3e6e583a0/6900e5aa71103d683f1d6990/openai-nvidia-markets.jpg?disable=upscale&width=1200&height=630&fit=crop&overlay=%2Fv3%2Fassets%2Fbltabaa95ef14172c61%2Fblt38d05c932b77fe9f%2F6a3931f66deb92be88b595a5%2FWM-OpenGraph_indigo.png&overlay-width=432&overlay-height=166&overlay-align=right,bottom

The August piece points the other way.
Assets have come down roughly $70 billion from the June peak, and the daily resets net sold about $150 billion of equity exposure between early June and July 29.
Lay the two reports on top of each other and one picture comes out.
Trading did not rise because new money arrived.
The money already there is changing hands more often.

## How memory reached 48%

Memory names account for 48% of the exposure inside single-stock long-leveraged ETFs.
Widen it to AI names and they are 58% of long-leveraged exposure, against 26% in 2022.

That matters because memory shares are a volatile asset to begin with.
Put a product that resets its multiple every day on top of a volatile stock, and the buying on up days and selling on down days lands as an extra layer on the move that was already there.

## The place Korea has already touched

The same article notes that leveraged ETF trading in South Korea fell away sharply after regulators stepped in.
How far this market can grow is set by rules as much as by demand for the product.

So how thick is the layer now sitting on top of the market.
If assets keep shrinking and the share of trading value comes down with them, June's heat is cooling off; if assets shrink while the share climbs further, the money left behind is spinning faster and widening the range inside the day.
In the first case the daily swings in memory shares settle down, and in the second the sharp moves near the close keep arriving with no earnings or industry news behind them.

What is at stake here is authority, not the rate.
Section 1012 of the federal tax code describes the purchase price of an asset only as its "cost."
The fight is over whether that word can be read as a number adjusted for inflation.

On September 1, 1992, Assistant Attorney General Timothy Flanigan of the Justice Department's Office of Legal Counsel issued an opinion.
It concluded that Treasury has no legal authority to index capital gains for inflation by regulation.
The reasoning was that "cost," in statutory language running back to 1918, means the price actually paid, and that Congress had chosen to handle inflation through preferential rates rather than through the purchase price.

The same idea came up during Trump's first term in 2019.
Treasury Secretary Steven Mnuchin said legislation should come first, and the idea quietly disappeared.

@@REF@@Conservatives eye Treasury action to index capital gains for inflation (Washington Examiner, 2026-07-17)|https://www.washingtonexaminer.com/policy/finance-and-economy/4652304/conservatives-eye-treasury-index-capital-gains-inflation/|https://www.washingtonexaminer.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/AP26148671840373.jpg?resize=1200,683

That piece walks through this year's revived push and adds one thing: after the 2024 Loper Bright ruling, courts no longer automatically defer to an agency's reading of a statute.
The same regulation would therefore be harder to defend in court than it would have been in 1992.
On March 6 this year, Representative Mark Alford and others wrote to Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent urging him to use existing executive authority.
How Treasury answered is not on the record.

## The scope decides the number

@@BAR@@Applied only to assets bought from now on|$170 billion|1700|Applied retroactively to assets already held|$1 trillion|10000@@These are the Budget Lab at Yale's estimates of lost revenue over ten years. The same policy changes size depending on whether assets already held are included.@@Checked 2026-08-12, Budget Lab at Yale, 2026-03-06

In the same work, households in the top 0.1 percent save roughly $350,000 on average, while the bottom 40 percent of earners get essentially nothing.
The break only appears when a long-held asset is sold.

Housing sits slightly apart.
Trump is also said to have floated exempting sales of homes worth $2 million or less.
The current exclusion on gains from a primary home is $250,000 for a single filer and $500,000 for a couple, set in 1997 and never indexed since.
That exclusion is the example the indexing camp reaches for most often.

## Before the November midterms, statute or regulation

If it arrives as a bill, the question is a vote count in Congress.
If it arrives as a Treasury regulation, it meets the 1992 opinion and Loper Bright from the day it takes effect.

So the life expectancy of this tax cut is set by its form rather than its rate.
As a regulation, even one in force leaves after-tax returns impossible to pencil in until the litigation ends; as legislation, passage itself is the answer.
Which of the two shows up is the thing to watch before November.

Samsung Electro-Mechanics has pushed the start of glass substrate mass production out to 2028.
The revision came less than a month after the company set up a joint venture and named the second half of 2027 as its start date.

@@REF@@Samsung Electro-Mechanics forms 480 billion won glass core joint venture with Sumitomo unit (The Korea Herald, 2026-07-02)|https://www.koreaherald.com/article/10796508|https://wimg.heraldcorp.com/news/cms/2026/07/02/news-p.v1.20260702.b8c4788347534b7eac4c178eb6471ef2_T1.jpg

The Korea Herald reported on July 2 that Samsung Electro-Mechanics was setting up a joint venture capitalized at 480 billion won with Dongwoo Fine-Chem, a subsidiary of Japan's Sumitomo Chemical.
Samsung Electro-Mechanics holds 66.2 percent and Dongwoo Fine-Chem 33.8 percent.
The plant goes inside Dongwoo Fine-Chem's Pyeongtaek campus, and the share purchase was set to close on September 1.

## Why glass substrates matter

The board a chip sits on is called a substrate.
Today it is built by stacking layers of a plastic-based material.

The wider you make that board, the more it bows, and heat makes it stretch.
The chip does not stretch, so when only the board does, the thousands of joints connecting the two go out of line.

Glass stays flat and stretches far less under heat.
That lets a package carry bigger chips packed closer together.
Put simply, the industry has been stacking heavy things on a soft wooden cutting board, and glass swaps that board for marble.

The catch is that glass cracks.
The customer who will buy the chips runs its own tests: hundreds of heat and cool cycles to see whether the board fractures, and pressure tests to see whether it holds.
That process is called reliability evaluation.

## The reliability evaluation is where this stopped

According to industry officials quoted in the original post, the halt came because Samsung Electro-Mechanics did not obtain reliability certification from a global communications chip customer.
The prototype has to be rebuilt and resubmitted, and because that cannot be done in a week or two, whether the line investment happens at all this year is now said to be uncertain.

The earlier three came with a new date attached; this one did not.@@Checked 2026-08-12, from the original post and Korea Herald reporting of 2026-07-02

@@REF@@Samsung Electro-Mechanics reportedly to form glass core JV with Sumitomo unit, targeting 2H27 production (TrendForce, 2026-07-06)|https://www.trendforce.com/news/2026/07/06/news-samsung-electro-mechanics-reportedly-signs-deal-to-form-glass-core-jv-with-sumitomo-unit-targeting-2h27-production/|https://img.trendforce.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/02172543/Samsung-Electro-Mechanics-624x468.png

TrendForce carried the same second-half-2027 target in a July 6 article.

## Deposition tools set the clock

Deposition equipment has the longest gap between order and delivery.
So the plan was to order deposition tools first, move the main process equipment into Pyeongtaek by April next year, and finish the initial line within the second quarter.
Allowing for how long the tools take to build, even an order placed this year leaves the line standing only in the second half of next year.

As recently as last month, equipment makers expected orders to start in August.

## If the deposition order lands inside 2026

If the deposition order goes out this year, the revised 2028 start holds.
If it does not, 2028 slips too.

The longer Samsung Electro-Mechanics is late, the longer anyone trying to build a bigger accelerator package has to keep using plastic-based boards.
The bowing problem grows with the size of the board, so the burden gets heavier the further out this runs.
Whether this is one company's delay, or a signal that glass substrates are a post-2028 story altogether, is decided by the same order.

Both stocks have multiplied several times over the past year.

A forward price-to-earnings ratio divides today's share price by the profit a company is expected to earn over the next twelve months.
A reading in the low fives means that buying the whole company at today's price would return the outlay in about six years of earnings.

hanke-yen-intervention-87b-is-an-estimat:
The $87 billion said to have been spent defending the yen is not a figure the Japanese government published.
It is an estimate, reconstructed by a private analyst from movements in the Bank of Japan's current account balances.

@@REF@@Japan and US confirm rare joint intervention to prop up yen (Al Jazeera, 2026-08-03)|https://www.aljazeera.com/economy/2026/8/3/japan-and-us-confirm-rare-joint-intervention-to-prop-up-yen|https://www.aljazeera.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/2026-08-02T233755Z_609247456_RC2NQMATKU91_RTRMADP_3_JAPAN-YEN-1785717755.jpg?resize=1920%2C1440

That the intervention happened is confirmed.
Japan and the US bought yen together across July 30 and 31, and on August 3 the finance authorities of both countries acknowledged it.
It was the first time the two had bought yen side by side since 1998.

## The finance ministry has released no number at all

Japan's Ministry of Finance discloses intervention amounts once a month as a range, and the exact day-by-day figures come later, in a quarterly release.
The most recent disclosure covers June 29 to July 29 and came out on July 31.
This intervention began the day after that window closed. The next release falls around September 1.

So that amount is, for now, a figure that cannot be checked.
Other estimates of the same two days differ. One puts Thursday alone near $59 billion; another splits it as roughly $75 billion from Japan and $5 to $10 billion from the US.
The estimates sit close to $10 billion apart from one another.

## Half of the gain has gone back

Just before the intervention the yen was at 163 to 164 per dollar, its weakest in forty years.
In the days after, it strengthened to 155.20.
On August 11 it stood at 159.25. It gained 8.8 yen and handed back 4.05, so 46% of the move is gone.

@@TIME@@July 30-31|Japan and the US buy yen across two days|August 3|Both governments confirm the joint operation; the yen reaches 155.20|August 11|159.25, roughly 46% of the gain returned|>Around September 1|Japan's finance ministry publishes the August intervention range|>September 17-18|Bank of Japan policy meeting@@What the market is waiting on is two things: confirmation of the amount, and the rate decision.@@Japan Ministry of Finance FX intervention disclosures; Bank of Japan meeting calendar

## Did the 1998 intervention work

In the joint operation of June 17, 1998, the US side spent $833 million.
The yen moved from 146.67 to 136.51 per dollar.
Two months later, in August, it was back at 147 to 148.

The trend broke in October of that year.
The Russian crisis and the collapse of a large hedge fund unwound, all at once, the trade of borrowing yen to buy other assets.
The intervention did not turn the direction; the direction turned only after the terms of borrowing changed.

@@REF@@Federal Reserve Bank of New York, Quarterly Report on Foreign Exchange Operations, Q2 1998 (New York Fed, 1998-08)|https://www.newyorkfed.org/medialibrary/media/newsevents/news/markets/1998/fxq298.pdf

The same pattern repeated in 2022 and 2024.
Japan spent 6.35 trillion yen alone in October 2022 and the yen still went through 150 afterwards, and the 9.79 trillion yen of April and May 2024 was retraced within two months.
What turned 2024 was the Bank of Japan raising rates at the end of July.

## What the September 18 Bank of Japan meeting will settle

So it is more useful to ask what makes an intervention hold than whether this one worked.
The US policy rate sits in the high 3% range; Japan's is 1%.
On ten-year government bonds it is 4.7% against 2.8%.

@@BAR@@US 10-year Treasury yield|4.7%|47|Japan 10-year government bond yield|2.8%|28@@Borrow in Japan, park it in US government bonds, and this much of a gap is still open. Intervention does not touch it.@@Checked 2026-08-11 · US 10-year from FRED DGS10; Japan 10-year at market close

While that gap stands, borrowing yen to hold another currency pays, and buying yen in the market does not remove the incentive.
How much was spent over those two days is settled around September 1. Whether the money meant anything is settled on September 18.
If the Bank of Japan lifts its policy rate above 1%, the job of holding the yen up passes from intervention to interest rates; if it holds, the yen's direction goes back to depending on US rates and on the ministry's next purchase.

The figure comes from the quarterly household debt report the New York Fed released on August 11.
Every three months it tallies what American households owe and how much of it has gone unpaid.

The phrase "90+ days delinquent" counts money, not people.
It does not tell you how many borrowers out of a hundred fell behind.
It tells you how many dollars out of every hundred lent have not come back for three months.

The same report carries other numbers.

## Why student loans rose alone

Student loans went from 10.3% to 10.6%.
What pushed that number up was not new borrowing but a rule.

During the pandemic the US paused repayment on federal student loans.
The pause ended in September 2023, and a further twelve-month cushion was attached to it right away.
Through those twelve months a missed payment was not reported to the credit bureaus.
Once that shield came off, years of unpaid balances began registering all at once.

That is why this line moves against the other two.@@New York Fed, Liberty Street Economics, 2026-05

## The bank ledger moves the other way

The household share sits high while the bank share comes down.
The charge-off rate on card loans at the 100 largest US banks fell from 4.3% in the first quarter of 2025 to 3.7% in the first quarter of 2026.
A charge-off is the share a bank has decided it will never collect and has erased from its books.

@@REF@@Americans' debt declines, but signs of financial strain persist (The National News Desk, 2026-08-11)|https://wcyb.com/news/nation-world/americans-debt-declines-but-signs-of-financial-strain-persist|https://wcyb.com/resources/media2/16x9/8119/1320/72x83/90/8ee95586-83e7-46d9-ac66-75da3f589f7c-GettyImages2288353363.jpg

That report settles on the same shape: the total fell while the marks of strain stayed.
The two numbers move apart for the reason set out above, that this measure counts dollars.
If the amount banks erase is shrinking while the share of late dollars stays high,
it reads as late money gathering more heavily on a smaller number of households.
That is the passage US coverage of this report labelled K-shaped.

## What the November New York Fed report will settle

So the question is whether to read these three numbers as an economy turning down, or as several years of record-keeping catching up.
On the evidence available, each is partly right.
The student loan rise is plainly the work of a rule, and card and auto turned direction from a high place.
Either way, the structure in which late money gathers on one side stays where it is.
The next place to see the same statistic is the 2026 Q3 report due in November.
If card delinquency 90+ falls below this quarter's reading, the decline was a trend; if it climbs above, the second quarter was a pause.

The trust fund behind US Social Security old-age benefits empties in the fourth quarter of 2032.
That lands several years before the 65-and-over population is projected to reach 78 million.
The population figures posted on August 11 have to be read next to that date.

@@BAR@@1990, actual|31.2 million|3120|2024, estimate|61.2 million|6120|2034, projection|77.0 million|7700@@Figures published by the US Census Bureau. ## Where the 66 million comes from

In the last population estimate the Census Bureau published, the 65-and-over population was 61.2 million, or 18.0 percent of the country.
That is the 2024 figure, released in June last year.

In 1990 it was 31.2 million, or 12.6 percent.
The count nearly doubled and the share rose by 5.4 percentage points.

The 66 million in the original post is a later estimate, and the 78 million in ten years is a projection.
In the Census Bureau's 2017 projections, the figure reaches 77.0 million around 2034, the year older adults first outnumber children under 18.

## The date that arrives before the people do

@@CHK@@Old-Age and Survivors Insurance trust fund depletion|Fourth quarter of 2032|Scheduled benefits payable at depletion|78%|Medicare Hospital Insurance fund depletion|2033@@These dates arrive before the population reaches 78 million. Absent a change in law, benefits pay out at 78 percent of what was promised from that point.@@Checked 2026-08-12, Social Security Administration 2026 Trustees Report, released 2026-06-09

The trust fund here works more like a bank balance than an endowment.
When payroll taxes collected in a year fall short of benefits paid that year, the difference is drawn from that balance.
When the balance hits zero the program does not disappear; it pays out only what came in that year.
Put simply, the doors do not close, but rationing starts.

At the end of 2025 there were roughly 70 million beneficiaries.

## Older Americans are already working longer

## The fourth quarter of 2032

Demographics move slowly and budgets move all at once.
So the number worth watching in this story is not 66 million or 78 million but the fourth quarter of 2032.

If next year's Trustees Report pushes that date back, wages and employment came in better than assumed; if it pulls the date forward, the number of people paying in is shrinking faster than assumed.
If the date holds, Treasury issuance and the argument over tax rates keep tightening toward it.
That America is aging is an old story, but the date the bill comes due is now six years out.
